content: Symptoms typically begin 3 to 14 days after infection.
They may include a high fever, headache, vomiting, muscle and joint pains, and a characteristic skin itching and skin rash.
Most cases of dengue fever are either asymptomatic or manifest mild symptoms such as an uncomplicated fever (80% of cases).

In severe dengue, symptoms include severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, rapid breathing, bleeding gums or nose, fatigue, restlessness, blood in vomit or stool, extreme thirst, pale and cold skin, and feelings of weakness.
Dengue virus is most frequently transmitted by the bite of mosquitos in the Aedes genus, particularly A. aegypti.
The virus has four confirmed serotypes; infection with one type usually gives lifelong immunity to that type, but only short-term immunity to the others.
Subsequent infection with a different type increases the risk of severe complications due to a phenomenon known as antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE).
Dengue fever vaccine, decreasing mosquito exposure.
Mosquito control is the primary method of prevention, including eliminating open sources of water and using insecticides or biological control agents.
Supportive care, intravenous fluids, blood transfusions.
For mild cases, treatment focuses on treating pain. Acetaminophen may be used to relieve mild fever or pain.
Severe dengue is a life-threatening emergency, requiring hospitalization and potentially intensive care.
As of March 2023, dengue is endemic in more than 100 countries with cases reported in every continent with the exception of Antarctica.
The Americas, Southeast Asia and the Western Pacific regions are the most seriously affected.
WHO currently estimates that 3.9 billion people are at risk of dengue infection.
Dengue has increased in incidence in recent decades, with WHO recording a ten fold increase between 2010 and 2019 (from 500,000 to 5 million recorded cases).
Infections are most commonly acquired in urban environments where the virus is primarily transmitted by the mosquito species Aedes aegypti.
Dengue is spreading from tropical and subtropical regions to the Iberian Peninsula and the southern states of the US, partly attributed to climate change.
Dengue has continued to increase in prevalence during the 21st century as the mosquito vector continues to expand its range.
